subject.title: [Feature]: read-only channel mode (inbound only, no outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw add a hard no-outbound channel/account contract for connected channels, and should that contract be WhatsApp-owned, shared across channel plugins, or delegated to external protocol isolation?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real and security-sensitive, but adding a config surface and suppressing outbound delivery changes channel API semantics and needs owner intent before automation picks an implementation boundary.

options.title: Approve account-level no-outbound mode
options.body: Define a stable account-level read-only/no-outbound contract, likely first in WhatsApp with a path to shared channel-plugin semantics, and require full send-path tests plus live proof.

options.title: Fold into listen-only/hooks-only design
options.body: Hold this issue until the broader hooks-only/no-agent mode in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78963 owns both inbound hook routing and outbound suppression semantics.

options.title: Delegate protocol isolation outside core
options.body: Prefer an external or plugin-owned isolation layer if maintainers do not want OpenClaw core/channel config to promise account-level transport silence.

recommendation.title: Approve account-level no-outbound mode
recommendation.body: Define a stable account-level read-only/no-outbound contract, likely first in WhatsApp with a path to shared channel-plugin semantics, and require full send-path tests plus live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent WhatsApp account/inbound history and were explicitly routed as WhatsApp expertise in related read-only PR discussion.
